It was an honor to welcome Yumi Otsuka, Woven by Toyota’s Corporate Adviser and Senior General Manager for Sustainability Management at Toyota Motor Corporation, to our Palo Alto office!
In a fireside chat with our Bay Area team, Otsuka-san shared her journey, from championing people-first workplace initiatives at Toyota to driving innovation at TOYOTA GAZOO Racing, along with why diverse perspectives matter. She then took the passenger seat to experience our latest automated driving developments.
We're grateful for her time and continued support of our mission.

What does it take to turn cutting-edge AI research into technology that works in the real world?
That was the question at the heart of AI DEV Day, hosted by our AI teams for engineers across Toyota group companies.
The event brought together:
🎤 Keynotes on the latest research and its path to practical applications
🧪 Hands-on demos of technologies in development
💬 Open discussion on how these technologies can make an impact
At Woven by Toyota, our AI teams are applying advanced AI to real-world challenges to help create healthier, more connected communities. From research to development, and from development to real-world impact, we're building technologies for well-being.
Want to build what comes next with us?

Woven by Toyota
September 25
One year ago, Woven City officially opened its doors. Today, it's a test course for mobility in motion.
Since launch, Toyota and Woven by Toyota have run close to 30 proof-of-concept trials with residents. The Inventor community also continues to grow, welcoming new partners across robotics, AI healthcare, sustainable resource circulation and mobility-energy platforms.
The city itself is also expanding: Phase 2 construction is underway, and starting next week, we're opening Woven City to visitors from across Japan.
And this is still just the beginning — with our Inventors and Weavers, we’ll keep building, testing and improving what comes next.
✅ Read the full year-one update: https://lnkd.in/gPS28DHe

September 25
How can we innovate mobility at scale while keeping people and safety at the center?
On September 30, our VP and Global Head of AD/ADAS, Dushyant Wadivkar, will take the stage at the A2TECH360 Mobility Summit, hosted by Ann Arbor SPARK.
In his keynote, “Innovating Mobility at Scale: Weaving AI, Safety, and Human-Centered Design,” Dushyant will share how Woven by Toyota is applying physical AI to help make mobility safer, smarter and more connected.
We’re looking forward to connecting with Michigan’s mobility community and exchanging ideas with the people shaping mobility’s next chapter at the American Center for Mobility.
Learn more and register: https://lnkd.in/g39iMbWG

Woven by Toyota is bringing together AI, automated driving technology, vehicle software, data, and human-centered design to help make mobility safer, smarter, and more connected.
On September 30, Dushyant Wadivkar, Vice President and Global Head of AD/ADAS at Woven by Toyota, will take the Ann Arbor Mobility Summit stage to share how the company is applying physical AI in driving environments where safety, reliability, and trust are essential — and how Toyota’s principle of Kaizen is helping turn continuous learning into real-world innovation.

September 17
Reflecting on yesterday’s fireside chat at the American Automotive Summit, I realized I kept coming back to one point.
Data-driven development is powerful, but it takes time and a ton of effort. The progress I see often comes from the less visible parts of the process like finding the right data, learning from failures, and improving how the system is evaluated.
Thank you to Alex Vogt from Inbolt for guiding the conversation, and to Kyle Hooper and the Generis team for bringing everyone together.
It was a pleasure to share ideas with others working toward safer and more enjoyable mobility.
